children: Bahrain's Electricity and Water Authority (EWA) has received two bids for a consultancy contract to develop electricity transmission infrastructure for the Khalifa City Housing Project.

The contract covers consultancy services for the establishment of two new 66-kilovolt (kV) substations to ensure electricity supply to the housing development, which is expected to be ready for occupancy between 2028 and 2030.

According to tender results published on 19 October 2026, AtkinsRéalis Major Projects submitted a bid of 493,680 Bahraini dinars ($1.31 million), while Energoprojekt Entel offered BHD 471,240 ($1.25 million).
AtkinsRéalis' bid was listed as accepted, while Energoprojekt Entel's lower-priced offer was marked as suspended.

The selected consultant will assess existing electricity systems, prepare designs and project plans, provide tendering and procurement support, manage contracts and supervise construction and implementation works.
The consultancy assignment forms part of EWA's preparations to provide electricity infrastructure for the Khalifa City Housing Project, which is being developed under Bahrain's Ministry of Housing.
(Writing by Deva Palanisamy; Editing by Anoop Menon)
